page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.large is a general-purpose, Nitro-based cloud instance designed around high-frequency processor execution. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8252C processor using the x86_64 architecture, delivering clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core across 2 hardware threads, backed by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 24 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (f and vnni), AES, and BMI2.

System memory consists of 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage through EBS. Network connectivity offers a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and graphics acceleration is absent with zero GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight an emphasis on single-threaded frequency over aggregate throughput. The high clock speed delivers strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.71 GB/sec and average single-core scores in stress-ng (1861.79) and Geekbench (1510.0). However, total throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU footprint, reflected in lower multicore rankings in Geekbench (1805.0), PassMark CPU (2908.48), and static web serving (2.49 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth metrics also register in the lower tiers.

The qualitative profile favors workloads where single-core processing limits execution time rather than parallel thread scalability. The m5zn.large is best suited for single-threaded batch tasks, small-scale relational databases, light compression pipelines, and general compute jobs requiring high instruction clock speeds.
